chunks: Muhammad ibn 'Abdillah ibn Ja'far Al-Himyari narrated to me from his father, from Harun ibn Muslim, from Al-Hasan ibn 'Ali, from Ahmad ibn 'A'idh, from Abu Ya'qub Al-Abzari, from Qa'id, from 'Abdillah ibn Salih (peace be upon him), who said:

I went to him and said to him, 'May I be sacrificed for you! Indeed, people are visiting Al-Husayn (peace be upon him), both those who know this matter and those who deny it, and women have traveled to him, and the state of fame/publicity has occurred. I have withdrawn from it because of the fame I saw.' He said, so he remained silent for a while not answering me. Then he turned to me and said, 'O Iraqi! If they have publicized themselves, do not publicize yourself. By Allah, no one who comes to Al-Husayn (peace be upon him) knowing his right will come except that Allah forgives him what preceded of his sin and what followed.'

key_terms.عَارِفٌ بِحَقِّهِ: One who knows his rights (referring to the Imam)
key_terms.مَا تَقَدَّمَ وَمَا تَأَخَّرَ: What preceded and what followed (past and future sins)

ai.seo_question: What is the spiritual reward for visiting Imam Al-Husayn (a.s.) with knowledge of his rights?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Kamil al-Ziyarat*, Imam al-Sadiq (a.s.) corrects the companion’s hesitation by distinguishing between the general public's superficial fame and the spiritual necessity of recognizing Imam al-Husayn’s specific rights (*haqq*). This highlights the Shia scholarly emphasis that the efficacy of Ziyarah lies not in the scale of attendance but in the visitor's conscious awareness of the Imam's status, promising comprehensive forgiveness for those who visit with this specific knowledge.

en.sayyid-mohsen-al-husayni-al-milani: 14. Muḥammad ibn ‘Abdillāh ibn Ja’far Al-Ḥimyari narrated to me from his father, from Hārūn ibn Muslim, from Ḥasan ibn ‘Ali, from Aḥmad ibn ‘Ā`idh, from Abī Ya’qūb Al-Abzāri, from Qā`id, who said:

I went to the Righteous Slave (Imam Kāżim (a.s.)) and said: May I sacrifice myself for you! (Many) people are going to the Ziyārah of Ḥusain (a.s.) from among those who believe in this matter and (among) those who deny it, and even women travel to him. It has become so widely-known (that) I have stopped going to him in fear of being identified. The Imam (a.s.) did not respond to me (immediately) and remained silent for some time. Then he (a.s.) looked toward me and said, “O Iraqi! Even if others go publicly, you should (still) go but do not identify yourself. I swear to Allāh that no one goes to the Ziyārah (a.s.) of Ḥusain knowing his rights without Allāh forgiving all of his past and future sins.”
